name: FL-23
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+9 district with strong Democratic baseline
No polling available, adding some uncertainty
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Frankel: a D+9 seat, incumbency, and a dominant fundraising edge over Adeimy, while Kalshi and Polymarket both price her near certain. With no polls to contradict this, the forecast stays at a roughly 20-point Democratic margin.
model.watch: A late influx of outside spending against Frankel or a polling surprise showing a much tighter race would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Lois Frankel seeks another term in a South Florida district that leans Democratic by about nine points. She enters the general election with a large financial advantage, holding roughly $1.2 million on hand after raising $2.3 million, while Republican challenger Deborah Adeimy has raised about $163,000 with modest reserves. Outside groups have spent little in the race so far.

Prediction markets on Kalshi and Polymarket both price Frankel's chances at 95 percent or higher, and no public general-election polling has emerged. The combination of the district's partisan lean, incumbency, and the money gap makes Frankel a heavy favorite, though the absence of polling leaves somewhat wider uncertainty than in well-surveyed races.
